title: [RPG Design Guides] Structuring the Protagonist and Companions

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】主人公と仲間の構成
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] Structuring the Protagonist and Companions

blocks.source: シナリオ面から見た主人公と仲間の構成に付いて考察する。
blocks.translation: This article examines the structure of the protagonist and companions from a story perspective.

blocks.source: 最初は主人公単独で書こうかと思ったけど、自然、仲間と関わってくる部分が非常に多いため、その関わりを中心にまとめてみた。基本的には仲間がある程度喋るタイプの作品を念頭に置いているので、そうでない場合はあまり役に立たないかも。
blocks.translation: At first, I considered writing about the protagonist alone, but there are naturally many aspects involving the companions, so I decided to focus on those relationships. I mainly have works in mind where the companions speak to some extent, so this may not be very useful otherwise.

blocks.source: ＲＰＧらしい冒険感を出すためには、やはり仲間の存在は不可欠。仲間との絆は物語において、当たり前のように使われるテーマである。絆を描くためにも、
blocks.translation: The presence of companions is essential for creating the sense of adventure characteristic of an RPG. The bond between companions is a theme commonly used in stories. To portray those bonds,

blocks.source: プレイヤー目線＝主人公目線から見て、心地良くて感情移入しやすい『おいしい人間関係』を構築してみよう。
blocks.translation: let's build enjoyable relationships that feel comfortable and easy to empathize with from the player's perspective—that is, the protagonist's perspective.

blocks.source: おいしい人間関係の例
blocks.translation: Examples of Enjoyable Relationships

blocks.source: 活躍する主人公
blocks.translation: A Protagonist Who Takes Center Stage

blocks.source: プレイヤーは自分＝主人公が活躍する物語を期待して、ゲームをプレイするもの。もちろん、主人公には、ちゃんと華を持たせてあげよう。
blocks.translation: Players play games expecting a story in which they—the protagonist—take center stage. Of course, make sure the protagonist gets their chance to shine.

blocks.source: そのための見せ方は様々だが、単純な方法だと『主人公特権』を与える手がある。
blocks.translation: There are many ways to do this, but one simple method is to give the protagonist “protagonist privileges.”

blocks.source: 例えば、以下のようなものが挙げられる。
blocks.translation: For example, these might include the following:

blocks.source: 強大な能力。極端な例だと、世界の命運を左右する様な物に。
blocks.translation: An overwhelming ability. In an extreme example, one that can determine the fate of the world.

blocks.source: 地位・血縁。国王・王子、伝説の勇者など。
blocks.translation: Status or lineage. Such as being a king, prince, or legendary Luminary.

blocks.source: 関係性。ヒロインやラスボス等の主要人物と強固な因縁を設定する。
blocks.translation: Relationships. Establishing a strong connection with a major character, such as the heroine or final boss.

blocks.source: このように、他のキャラクターでは敵わないような特権を主人公に与えることで、必然的に物語の中心に置き、活躍させることができる。特権は最初から持っている場合と、途中で手に入れる場合の二通りがあるので、話に合わせて考えよう。
blocks.translation: By giving the protagonist privileges that other characters cannot match in this way, you can naturally place them at the center of the story and let them take an active role. There are two possibilities: the protagonist may have these privileges from the beginning, or acquire them along the way. Consider which works best for your story.

blocks.source: とはいえ、こんな安直な方法は嫌だという人もいるかもしれないし、主人公特権に頼らずとも活躍させることは可能だ。
blocks.translation: That said, some people may dislike such a straightforward approach, and it is possible to make the protagonist shine without relying on protagonist privileges.

blocks.source: 普通の人間が頑張る話を描きたい場合は、強力過ぎる特権は必要ない。ただし、その場合は主人公の影が薄くならないように配慮がより必要となる。
blocks.translation: If you want to portray an ordinary person working hard, there is no need for overly powerful privileges. However, in that case, you need to take greater care to ensure that the protagonist does not fade into the background.

blocks.source: 周りから好かれる主人公
blocks.translation: A Protagonist Who Is Loved by Those Around Them

blocks.source: 『愛情』『友情』『家族愛』『信頼』など色々考えられるが、周りの仲間が主人公へ対して好意を持っている描写を行う。
blocks.translation: There are many possibilities, such as “love,” “friendship,” “familial love,” and “trust,” but show the companions around the protagonist feeling affection for them.

blocks.source: 物語開始時点から、いきなり好意を持たれているよりも、
blocks.translation: Rather than having the protagonist suddenly be liked from the very beginning of the story,

blocks.source: 物語を進行させるに伴い、徐々に好意を持たれるという過程を描写した方がより感情移入しやすい。
blocks.translation: it is easier for players to empathize when you portray the process of the protagonist gradually earning that affection as the story progresses.

blocks.source: 時々、主人公の相手となるヒロインを戦闘可能な仲間ではなく外に置く作品（ＤＱ８、１１、ワイルドアームズ２など）があるけれど、基本的には、パーティ内に組み込んだ方がプレイヤーからの好感度は高くなりやすい。
blocks.translation: Sometimes, a heroine who is the protagonist's love interest is kept outside the party rather than made into a battle-capable companion (as in DQ8, DQ11, and Wild Arms 2), but generally, including her in the party makes it easier for players to develop favorable feelings toward her.

blocks.source: そのほうが、イベントでの出番が増えるし、戦闘などのゲーム部分を通じても、プレイヤーがヒロインに対して、愛着を持つ効果が期待できる。
blocks.translation: This gives her more appearances in events, and players can also be expected to grow attached to her through gameplay elements such as battles.

blocks.source: これはゲームという双方性を持った媒体ならではの効果といえる。ゲーム的には、戦闘メンバーの一枠を占めてしまう問題もあるけれど……。
blocks.translation: This could be called an effect unique to games as an interactive medium. From a gameplay perspective, though, it does mean that she takes up one slot in the battle party…

blocks.source: また「周りから好かれる」と書いたけれど、主に重要なのは仲間からの好意である。それ以外の人物については、この限りではない。
blocks.translation: I wrote “loved by those around them,” but what matters most is affection from the companions. This does not necessarily apply to everyone else.

blocks.source: 例えば、主人公はわけあって、町の人間から忌み嫌われているが、「それでも、主人公のことを信じ、頼りにしてくれる仲間がいる」というシチュエーションも中々ポイントが高い。
blocks.translation: For example, the protagonist may be despised by the townspeople for some reason, yet the situation where “there are still companions who believe in and rely on the protagonist” can be quite compelling.

blocks.source: もちろん、様々な問題を解決する中で、町人からの信頼を得ていくという王道スタイルも悪くない。
blocks.translation: Of course, the classic approach of earning the townspeople's trust by solving various problems is also a good one.

blocks.source: 良好な人間関係
blocks.translation: Good Relationships

blocks.source: 主人公以外の仲間に関しても、同じようにして良好な人間関係を構成させよう。感動的なエンディングを迎えるためにも麗しい仲間関係を築きたい。人間関係の具体的な構成方法に付いては、詳細を後述する。
blocks.translation: The same approach should be used to create good relationships among the companions other than the protagonist. Building warm bonds among the companions is important for achieving a moving ending. I will discuss specific ways to structure these relationships in more detail later.

blocks.source: まずい人間関係の例
blocks.translation: Examples of Bad Relationships

blocks.source: 主人公が空気
blocks.translation: A Protagonist Who Fades into the Background

blocks.source: 『活躍する主人公』『周りから好かれる主人公』の正反対。主人公に感情移入していたプレイヤーは、むなしくなること請け合い。特に無口主人公の作品で、仲間同士の会話が多い作品では注意が必要となる。
blocks.translation: The exact opposite of “a protagonist who takes center stage” and “a protagonist who is loved by those around them.” Players who had empathized with the protagonist are sure to feel empty. This requires particular caution in works with a silent protagonist and lots of conversations between companions.

blocks.source: これを書いてる当人も若干空気主人公をやらかしている気がしないでもないです。まずってたら反面教師だと思ってください。
blocks.translation: I have a feeling that I, the person writing this, have also made the protagonist fade into the background to some extent. If I have made a mistake, please treat me as a cautionary example.

blocks.source: ぎこちない人間関係
blocks.translation: Awkward Relationships

blocks.source: 序盤～中盤に、後の展開への布石としてやるのは問題ないと思う。しかし、物語終盤になっても、人間関係がぎこちないのは勘弁。
blocks.translation: I think this is fine in the early to middle part of the story as groundwork for later developments. However, please spare me relationships that are still awkward near the end of the story.

blocks.source: パーティ内でカップル成立。しかし主人公は一人孤独
blocks.translation: A Couple Forms within the Party, Leaving the Protagonist Alone

blocks.source: 言うまでもなく心理的にかなり嫌な状況。リア充爆発しろ。
blocks.translation: Needless to say, this is a psychologically unpleasant situation. Damn those happy couples.

blocks.source: このように仲間同士に強すぎる絆を設定すると、主人公が空気化する懸念も。主人公にも何らかの絆を設定してあげたいところ。
blocks.translation: If you establish bonds that are too strong between the companions, as in this example, the protagonist may fade into the background. It would be best to give the protagonist some kind of bond as well.

blocks.source: 物語当初から成立している相思相愛の恋愛関係
blocks.translation: A Mutual Romantic Relationship Established from the Beginning of the Story

blocks.source: 主人公とヒロイン等の恋愛関係が、物語開始時点で既に成立していた場合の問題点。これは、主人公視点で考えれば「モテモテでいいじゃないか」と思えるかもしれないけど、プレイヤー視点ではそうはいかない。感情移入を妨げる結構な危険性を持っている。
blocks.translation: This is the problem that arises when a romantic relationship between the protagonist and heroine, for example, is already established when the story begins. From the protagonist's perspective, one might think, “What's wrong with being popular?” But it does not work that way from the player's perspective. It carries a considerable risk of preventing players from empathizing with the characters.

blocks.source: 長い物語を進める中で、主人公とヒロインは仲を深めていくのが正道。
blocks.translation: The proper approach is for the protagonist and heroine to grow closer as the long story unfolds.

blocks.source: その過程を体験することで、プレイヤーは主人公やヒロインに感情移入をしたり、好意を持ったりする。ここの部分の描写は結構難しく、「ヒロインが嫌い」なんて理由で、作品自体が叩かれていることも珍しくない。
blocks.translation: By experiencing that process, players empathize with the protagonist and heroine and develop affection for them. Portraying this part is quite difficult, and it is not uncommon for an entire work to be criticized because “I hate the heroine.”

blocks.source: ただでさえ、恋愛関係の描写は扱いが難しいのだが、当初から、主人公とヒロインの関係が成立していた場合は問題がさらに深い。
blocks.translation: Portraying romantic relationships is difficult enough as it is, but the problem becomes even more serious when the relationship between the protagonist and heroine is already established from the beginning.

blocks.source: なんせ、大事な部分の過程を無視することになる。
blocks.translation: After all, this means skipping over the process that matters most.

blocks.source: 当然、プレイヤーは主人公程にはヒロインのことを好きになれない可能性が高くなるし、そのヒロインを好きな主人公に対して、プレイヤーが感情移入することも難しくなる。
blocks.translation: Naturally, players are then less likely to come to love the heroine as much as the protagonist does, and it also becomes difficult for them to empathize with a protagonist who loves her.

blocks.source: 開始時点での主人公とヒロインの関係は、仲が良い幼馴染ぐらいが無難と思う。……そもそも、無理に恋愛を絡めなくてよいけど。
blocks.translation: At the beginning, it seems safest for the protagonist and heroine to be no more than close childhood friends. …Though there is no need to force romance into the story in the first place.

blocks.source: 物語当初からのリア充
blocks.translation: A Protagonist Who Already Has It All from the Start

blocks.source: 同様の理由で、主人公が物語開始時点で既に多くの仲間キャラと親しい、といったリア充的な設定も難しい。
blocks.translation: For the same reason, it is difficult to make the protagonist someone who is already close to many companion characters when the story begins—a protagonist who already has it all.

blocks.source: やはり、過程を飛ばした人間関係はプレイヤー目線では感情移入し辛い。それに、余りにも最初から数が多いとプレイヤーがキャラを把握するのにも疲れる。兄弟・幼馴染など、最初から仲の良い仲間キャラもいてよいけれど、２～３人程度で十分だろう。
blocks.translation: As expected, relationships that skip the process of becoming close are difficult for players to empathize with. Besides, if there are too many companions from the start, players will get tired trying to keep track of them all. It is fine to have some companions who are already close to the protagonist, such as siblings or childhood friends, but two or three should be enough.

blocks.source: 余談だけど、ＲＰＧの主人公に１０～２０代が多いのは、対象プレイヤーの年齢を考慮しているというのも、もちろんあるが、同時に若くて真っさらな人間の方が「感情移入しやすい」「前提情報が少なく導入がスムーズ」という理由が大きいと思う。
blocks.translation: As an aside, the reason RPG protagonists are often in their teens or twenties is, of course, partly due to the target players' ages. But I think the bigger reasons are that younger, unformed people are “easier to empathize with” and that “having less background information makes the introduction smoother.”

blocks.source: もっとも、３０代以降の主人公を全否定するわけでもない。
blocks.translation: That said, I am not rejecting protagonists in their thirties or older outright.

blocks.source: 少し表現が難しくなるかもしれないが、人がやらないことをやるのは差別化にもなる。影のある歴戦の剣士が主人公で、物語の進行と共に徐々にその過去が明らかになるといった設定も十分可能だろう。
blocks.translation: It may be somewhat difficult to portray, but doing something others do not is also a way to stand out. A sufficiently viable premise would be to make the protagonist a battle-hardened swordsman with a troubled past, which is gradually revealed as the story progresses.

blocks.source: 仲間キャラクターには明確な個性付けを
blocks.translation: Give Your Party Members Distinct Personalities

blocks.source: 仲間キャラクターには明確な個性付けをした上で、それぞれの個性は分散させよう。色々なキャラクターがいたほうが物語の幅が広がるし、華が出る。作者にとっても引き出しを増やす効果がある。
blocks.translation: Give your party members clear, distinct personalities, and make sure those personalities are varied. Having a diverse cast broadens the scope of the story and adds flair. It also gives the author more creative options.

blocks.source: また、性格に特徴のないキャラクターや、似たような性格のキャラクターが集まると、単純に区別が付きにくい。
blocks.translation: Also, when characters with no notable personality traits or with similar personalities are gathered together, they naturally become difficult to distinguish.

blocks.source: セリフも各自の口調や一人称（俺、僕、私、あたし……）を分散させた方が、すぐに見分けが付くので読みやすい。小説でもゲームでも、各セリフを誰が発したか解読に時間を要するような作品は苦痛なもの。
blocks.translation: Their speech patterns and first-person pronouns (I, me, etc.) should also be varied, making them easy to tell apart and the story easier to read. Whether in novels or games, works where it takes time to figure out who said each line are painful to experience.

blocks.source: 各キャラクターの個性付けは、基本的には『熱血』『冷静』『お転婆』『温厚』『博識』『へたれ』『天然』『寡黙』といった単純な分類で構わない。その上で、性格に深みを出せるかどうかは、作者の腕次第。
blocks.translation: Character personalities can basically be based on simple categories such as “hot-blooded,” “calm,” “tomboyish,” “gentle,” “knowledgeable,” “weak-willed,” “airheaded,” and “taciturn.” From there, whether you can give those personalities depth depends on the author’s skill.

blocks.source: 「単純な分類」＝「安直なキャラ付け」というわけではないので注意したい。
blocks.translation: Keep in mind that “simple categories” do not necessarily mean “superficial characterization.”

blocks.source: 例えば、いくら熱血キャラだからといっても「敵に真正面から突っ込んで、事態を悪化させる」といった行動を学習なく、何度も取られると、さすがにゲンナリしてしまう。ギャグキャラとしてならアリかもしれないけれど……。
blocks.translation: For example, no matter how hot-blooded a character is, if they repeatedly charge straight at the enemy and make matters worse without learning from their mistakes, you will eventually grow tired of it. It might work for a comedic character, though…

blocks.source: あくまでも人間として、自然な思考や行動をさせることが原則。
blocks.translation: The basic principle is to have them think and act naturally, as human beings.

blocks.source: 各キャラが取る言動は「自分ならどうする？」を基準にすればよいと思う。そこから、余りにもかけ離れた言動は、いくら創作上のキャラだからといっても、安易に取らせないほうが無難だろう。
blocks.translation: I think the standard for each character’s words and actions should be, “What would I do?” Even for a fictional character, it is probably safest not to have them casually say or do things that are too far removed from that.

blocks.source: 物語を動かすために、時には強引な行動をさせる必要もあるかもしれないが、そのポイントは絞るようにしよう。例えば序盤、キャラクターの未熟さを表現するために、あえてプレイヤーの反感を買うような言動を取らせる手法もある。
blocks.translation: You may sometimes need to have characters take forceful actions to move the story forward, but try to limit those instances. For example, early on, you can deliberately have a character say or do something that turns the player against them in order to portray their immaturity.

blocks.source: また、別にプレイヤーに嫌われてもよいキャラクターならば、割りきって、ストーリーの都合に合わせて、好き勝手するのもよいかもしれない。
blocks.translation: On the other hand, if a character is not meant to be liked by the players, you might as well have them do whatever they want to suit the needs of the story.

blocks.source: パーティの人間関係の構成
blocks.translation: Structuring Relationships Within the Party

blocks.source: 具体的に、どのようにパーティの人間関係を構成していくかを考える。大事なのは各キャラクターの役割を分散させて被らないようにすること。二通りの方法を考えてみた。
blocks.translation: Let’s consider specifically how to structure relationships within the party. The important thing is to distribute each character’s role so that none of them overlap. I came up with two approaches.

blocks.source: 家族に例えて構成する
blocks.translation: Structure the Party as a Family

blocks.source: パーティメンバーの年齢がバラバラの場合は、それぞれを家族に当てはめると、バランスの取れた構成になる。
blocks.translation: When the party members vary in age, assigning each of them a family role creates a well-balanced group.

blocks.source: 主人公とヒロインを中心に見て、各仲間が以下のようなポジションに当てはまるように構成すると、役割が被り辛くなる。
blocks.translation: Centering on the protagonist and heroine, assign each companion one of the following positions to help prevent their roles from overlapping.

blocks.source: 主人公
blocks.translation: Protagonist

blocks.source: パーティの中心として皆を主導する。
blocks.translation: Leads everyone as the center of the party.

blocks.source: ヒロイン
blocks.translation: Heroine

blocks.source: メインヒロイン。
blocks.translation: The main heroine.

blocks.source: 主人公の不動のパートナー。
blocks.translation: The protagonist’s steadfast partner.

blocks.source: 父
blocks.translation: Father

blocks.source: パーティで年長の男性。
blocks.translation: The oldest man in the party.

blocks.source: 物語のキーマンとして、パーティを監督する率が高い気がする。
blocks.translation: As a key figure in the story, he often seems to supervise the party.

blocks.source: 母
blocks.translation: Mother

blocks.source: パーティで年長の女性。
blocks.translation: The oldest woman in the party.

blocks.source: あんまり出てこない。
blocks.translation: She does not appear very often.

blocks.source: 兄
blocks.translation: Older Brother

blocks.source: 主人公より年上の男性。
blocks.translation: A man older than the protagonist.

blocks.source: 父に近い役割を果たすこともあれば、親友格だったりする場合も。
blocks.translation: Sometimes he serves a role similar to the father’s, while in other cases he is more like a best friend.

blocks.source: 姉
blocks.translation: Older Sister

blocks.source: ヒロインより年上の女性。
blocks.translation: A woman older than the heroine.

blocks.source: 冷静な知恵役だったり、姉御肌だったり。
blocks.translation: She may be the calm, wise one or have a protective big-sister personality.

blocks.source: 弟
blocks.translation: Younger Brother

blocks.source: 主人公より年下の男性。
blocks.translation: A man younger than the protagonist.

blocks.source: ヤンチャだったり、いじられ役だったり。
blocks.translation: He may be mischievous or serve as the butt of jokes.

blocks.source: 妹
blocks.translation: Younger Sister

blocks.source: ヒロインより年下の女性。
blocks.translation: A woman younger than the heroine.

blocks.source: ムードメーカー。割りと美味しいポジション。
blocks.translation: The mood-maker. A fairly desirable position.

blocks.source: ペット
blocks.translation: Pet

blocks.source: 人外。
blocks.translation: A non-human character.

blocks.source: 重要な役割を果たす異種族だったり、単なるマスコットだったりと色々と自由に設定できる。
blocks.translation: This role can be freely defined in many ways, from a member of another race who plays an important role to a simple mascot.

blocks.source: 以上は目安だが、最終的なパーティ人数によっても、構成は変わってくるので柔軟に考えよう。「父と兄」「母と姉」など、役割が被っている箇所は統合しやすい。主人公やヒロイン自身を兄姉弟妹のいずれかに当てはめても構わない。
blocks.translation: The above is only a guideline, and the structure will also change depending on the final party size, so be flexible. Overlapping roles, such as “father and older brother” or “mother and older sister,” are easy to combine. You can also assign the protagonist or heroine one of the older or younger sibling roles.

blocks.source: 役割を元に構成する
blocks.translation: Structure the Party Around Roles

blocks.source: 次に役割を元にパーティ構成を考えてみる。
blocks.translation: Next, let’s consider structuring the party around roles.

blocks.source: とりあえずは、下のような感じで分類してみた。分類名の一部は良い言葉がなかったので適当に考えた。家族による構成と併せて、うまくキャラに役割を持たせていこう。
blocks.translation: For now, I classified them roughly as shown below. I came up with some of the category names arbitrarily because I could not find better terms. Along with the family-based structure, let’s give each character an appropriate role.

blocks.source: 主観者
blocks.translation: Viewpoint Character

blocks.source: プレイヤーの視点となる人物。
blocks.translation: The character who serves as the player’s point of view.

blocks.source: 基本は主人公だがＤＱ４のように進行に応じて変化する場合も。
blocks.translation: Usually this is the protagonist, but it may change as the story progresses, as in Dragon Quest IV.

blocks.source: シャーロック・ホームズにおけるワトスンのように、物語の中心から外れた人物に固定する場合もあるが、性質上ＲＰＧには不向き。
blocks.translation: In some cases, this role is fixed to a character outside the center of the story, like Watson in Sherlock Holmes, but by its nature, it is ill-suited to RPGs.

blocks.source: 目的役
blocks.translation: Purpose Role

blocks.source: 物語の目的に最も強く関わる人物。
blocks.translation: The character most strongly connected to the purpose of the story.

blocks.source: 主人公あるいはヒロイン。西遊記では三蔵法師に当たる。
blocks.translation: The protagonist or heroine. In Journey to the West, this role is played by Xuanzang.

blocks.source: 主導者
blocks.translation: Leader

blocks.source: 物語の目的を果たすために、実際にパーティを主導しながら活躍する人物。
blocks.translation: The character who actively contributes while actually leading the party in order to fulfill the purpose of the story.

blocks.source: ＲＰＧにおいては、プレイヤーが操作するキャラクター（＝主観者）に等しい場合が普通。これは当然、主人公にやって貰わないと困る。『目的役』のヒロインが持つ目的を達成するために、主人公が頑張るという構図は鉄板。
blocks.translation: In RPGs, this role is usually equivalent to the character controlled by the player (i.e., the viewpoint character). Naturally, it would be a problem if the protagonist did not fill this role. A classic setup is for the protagonist to work hard to fulfill the purpose held by the heroine in the “purpose role.”

blocks.source: 保護者
blocks.translation: Guardian

blocks.source: 直接パーティを主導しないが、主人公を初めとしたパーティメンバーを指導・補佐する役割。
blocks.translation: A character who does not directly lead the party, but guides and supports the party members, including the protagonist.

blocks.source: 基本的に主人公より年上。
blocks.translation: Basically older than the protagonist.

blocks.source: 従者
blocks.translation: Attendant

blocks.source: 主人公（またはヒロイン）に付き従う者。
blocks.translation: Someone who follows the protagonist (or heroine).

blocks.source: 主人公の身分が高い場合は文字通りの従者（護衛やメイドなど）がいることが多い。その他にも弟や妹、子分なども含まれる。
blocks.translation: When the protagonist has high social status, they often have literal attendants, such as guards or maids. This category can also include younger brothers or sisters and underlings.

blocks.source: 感想役
blocks.translation: Commentator

blocks.source: 物事に対して感想を述べる役割。それによって、プレイヤーが話に付いて行きやすいようにする。
blocks.translation: A character whose role is to comment on events. This makes it easier for the player to follow the story.

blocks.source: 思ったことを、そのまま口にするような率直なキャラのほうがよいかも。
blocks.translation: A straightforward character who says exactly what they think may work best.

blocks.source: 知恵袋
blocks.translation: Brains

blocks.source: 問題を整理・解決するために知恵を出す役目。
blocks.translation: The character whose role is to provide wisdom for organizing and solving problems.

blocks.source: 冷静な分析をするタイプもいれば、科学等の技術によって物事を解決するタイプも。『感想役』とのやり取りによって、プレイヤーへ状況を分かりやすく伝えることが多い。
blocks.translation: Some are the type to perform calm analyses, while others solve problems through science and other technologies. Exchanges with the “commentator” often help explain the situation to the player in an easy-to-understand way.

blocks.source: 感想役「どういうことだってばよ！？」
blocks.translation: Commentator: “What the heck does that mean!?”

blocks.source: 知恵袋「つまり――（以降解説）」
blocks.translation: Brains: “In other words—(explanation continues)”

blocks.source: トリックスター
blocks.translation: Trickster

blocks.source: 「故意にイタズラする」「うかつな行動を取る」などして物語を引っ掻き回す。
blocks.translation: They stir up the story by doing things such as “deliberately playing pranks” or “acting carelessly.”

blocks.source: 高い行動力で、既存の秩序を破壊し、新たな局面を導き出すという主人公属性的な側面も併せ持つ。
blocks.translation: They also have an aspect of the protagonist archetype: through their high initiative, they destroy the existing order and bring about a new turn of events.

blocks.source: 最初は敵側として登場するキャラなどによいかも。
blocks.translation: This may work well for a character who initially appears on the enemy’s side, for example.

blocks.source: にぎやかし
blocks.translation: Comic Relief

blocks.source: 物語の進行には関わらないところで、物語・会話を盛り上げる役目を持つ。明るいキャラの見せ場。
blocks.translation: This character’s role is to liven up the story and conversations outside the actual progression of the plot. It is a chance for the cheerful character to shine.

blocks.source: 『いじられ役』などもこれに含んでよいかも。
blocks.translation: The “butt of the joke” role may also fit into this category.

blocks.source: 一つのキャラクターが複数の役割を持つ場合もあれば、複数のキャラクターが一つの役目を持つ場合もある。ただし、余り多くのキャラで役割が被るのはよくない。
blocks.translation: Sometimes one character has multiple roles, while other times multiple characters share a single role. However, it is best not to have too many characters overlap in their roles.

blocks.source: また、物語が進むに連れて役割が移っていくことも多い。例えば、最初は未熟で『主観者』に過ぎなかった主人公が成長するに伴い『主導者』として、仲間を導くようになるなど。
blocks.translation: Roles also often shift as the story progresses. For example, as an initially inexperienced protagonist who was nothing more than a “viewpoint character” grows, they may become a “leader” who guides their companions.

blocks.source: 「うまく役割を与えられなかったキャラ」や「仲の良い相手がいないキャラ」「戦闘で使われないキャラ」は空気になりやすいので注意。特に登場が遅いキャラクターは『役割』『仲の良さ』『戦闘』のどの面でも先行キャラに負けて、不遇になりやすい。
blocks.translation: Be careful, because “characters who were not given suitable roles,” “characters who have no close relationships,” and “characters who are not used in battle” tend to fade into the background. Characters who appear particularly late are likely to be treated unfairly, losing out to earlier characters in terms of “roles,” “friendships,” and “combat.”

blocks.source: 会話システム
blocks.translation: Conversation Systems

blocks.source: ＤＱ７～８の『話す』やテイルズオブの『チャット』など、本筋を進めるには必要でない仲間との会話をシステムとして、組み込んでいる作品もある。このようにして、キャラクターの個性を強調する方法もある。一応、知らない人のために説明すると……
blocks.translation: Some games incorporate conversations with party members that are not necessary for progressing the main story as a system, such as the “Talk” feature in DQ7–8 and the “Skits” in Tales of games. This is one way to emphasize the characters’ personalities. For those unfamiliar with them, here is a brief explanation…

blocks.source: 話す
blocks.translation: Talk

blocks.source: 主人公が仲間から話を聞き出すという一対一の会話。無口主人公ならば、選択肢を除いて、仲間からの一方通行の会話となる。無口主人公は『チャット』に参加できないので、必然的にこちらを推奨。
blocks.translation: A one-on-one conversation in which the protagonist draws information out of a party member. With a silent protagonist, aside from choices, the conversation becomes one-way, with the party member doing all the talking. Since a silent protagonist cannot participate in “Skits,” this option is naturally recommended.

blocks.source: チャット
blocks.translation: Skits

blocks.source: 複数の仲間同士でのワイワイした会話。パーティ内での関係性・仲の良さなどを強調することができる。
blocks.translation: Lively conversations among multiple party members. These can emphasize the relationships and friendships within the party.

blocks.source: いずれにせよ、作業量は半端ないので注意。長編ＲＰＧでこんなシステムを導入すると、テキスト量は、本編と合わせて、まず確実に小説一冊分（１５万字～）を越えることになる。
blocks.translation: In any case, be warned that the amount of work involved is enormous. If you introduce a system like this in a long RPG, the total amount of text, including the main story, will almost certainly exceed the length of a novel (150,000 characters or more).

blocks.source: まとめ
blocks.translation: Conclusion

blocks.source: 漫画などは連載が続く中で、無闇にキャラが増加する傾向がある。
blocks.translation: Manga and similar works tend to add characters indiscriminately as serialization continues.

blocks.source: 結果、存在感のないキャラが増えたり、無理に全員に見せ場を作って、テンポが悪くなるといった状況が見られる。ゲームの場合は連載ではないので、こういった心配はない。全体の構成を考えて必要なメンバーを考えよう。
blocks.translation: As a result, they may end up with more characters who lack presence, or the pacing may suffer because the creators force themselves to give every character a chance to shine. Games are not serialized, so this is not something you need to worry about. Consider the overall structure and determine which members are necessary.

lines.translation: [[LINK_1]]>Return to the RPG Design Guides index[[/LINK_1]]

texts.シナリオ面から見た主人公と仲間の構成に付いて考察する。: This article examines the structure of the protagonist and companions from a story perspective.
texts.最初は主人公単独で書こうかと思ったけど、自然、仲間と関わってくる部分が非常に多い: At first, I considered writing about the protagonist alone, but there are naturally many aspects involving the companions, so I decided to focus on those relationships. I mainly have works in mind where the companions speak to some extent, so this may not be very useful otherwise.
texts.ＲＰＧらしい冒険感を出すためには、やはり仲間の存在は不可欠。仲間との絆は物語にお: The presence of companions is essential for creating the sense of adventure characteristic of an RPG. The bond between companions is a theme commonly used in stories. To portray those bonds,
texts.プレイヤー目線＝主人公目線から見て、心地良くて感情移入しやすい『おいしい人間関係: let's build enjoyable relationships that feel comfortable and easy to empathize with from the player's perspective—that is, the protagonist's perspective.
texts.活躍する主人公: A Protagonist Who Takes Center Stage
texts.プレイヤーは自分＝主人公が活躍する物語を期待して、ゲームをプレイするもの。もちろ: Players play games expecting a story in which they—the protagonist—take center stage. Of course, make sure the protagonist gets their chance to shine.
texts.そのための見せ方は様々だが、単純な方法だと『主人公特権』を与える手がある。: There are many ways to do this, but one simple method is to give the protagonist “protagonist privileges.”
texts.例えば、以下のようなものが挙げられる。: For example, these might include the following:
texts.強大な能力。極端な例だと、世界の命運を左右する様な物に。: An overwhelming ability. In an extreme example, one that can determine the fate of the world.
texts.地位・血縁。国王・王子、伝説の勇者など。: Status or lineage. Such as being a king, prince, or legendary Luminary.
texts.関係性。ヒロインやラスボス等の主要人物と強固な因縁を設定する。: Relationships. Establishing a strong connection with a major character, such as the heroine or final boss.
texts.このように、他のキャラクターでは敵わないような特権を主人公に与えることで、必然的: By giving the protagonist privileges that other characters cannot match in this way, you can naturally place them at the center of the story and let them take an active role. There are two possibilities: the protagonist may have these privileges from the beginning, or acquire them along the way. Consider which works best for your story.
texts.とはいえ、こんな安直な方法は嫌だという人もいるかもしれないし、主人公特権に頼らず: That said, some people may dislike such a straightforward approach, and it is possible to make the protagonist shine without relying on protagonist privileges.
texts.普通の人間が頑張る話を描きたい場合は、強力過ぎる特権は必要ない。ただし、その場合: If you want to portray an ordinary person working hard, there is no need for overly powerful privileges. However, in that case, you need to take greater care to ensure that the protagonist does not fade into the background.
texts.周りから好かれる主人公: A Protagonist Who Is Loved by Those Around Them
texts.『愛情』『友情』『家族愛』『信頼』など色々考えられるが、周りの仲間が主人公へ対し: There are many possibilities, such as “love,” “friendship,” “familial love,” and “trust,” but show the companions around the protagonist feeling affection for them.
texts.物語開始時点から、いきなり好意を持たれているよりも、: Rather than having the protagonist suddenly be liked from the very beginning of the story,
texts.物語を進行させるに伴い、徐々に好意を持たれるという過程を描写した方がより感情移入: it is easier for players to empathize when you portray the process of the protagonist gradually earning that affection as the story progresses.
texts.時々、主人公の相手となるヒロインを戦闘可能な仲間ではなく外に置く作品（ＤＱ８、１: Sometimes, a heroine who is the protagonist's love interest is kept outside the party rather than made into a battle-capable companion (as in DQ8, DQ11, and Wild Arms 2), but generally, including her in the party makes it easier for players to develop favorable feelings toward her.
texts.そのほうが、イベントでの出番が増えるし、戦闘などのゲーム部分を通じても、プレイヤ: This gives her more appearances in events, and players can also be expected to grow attached to her through gameplay elements such as battles.
texts.これはゲームという双方性を持った媒体ならではの効果といえる。ゲーム的には、戦闘メ: This could be called an effect unique to games as an interactive medium. From a gameplay perspective, though, it does mean that she takes up one slot in the battle party…
texts.また「周りから好かれる」と書いたけれど、主に重要なのは仲間からの好意である。それ: I wrote “loved by those around them,” but what matters most is affection from the companions. This does not necessarily apply to everyone else.
texts.例えば、主人公はわけあって、町の人間から忌み嫌われているが、「それでも、主人公の: For example, the protagonist may be despised by the townspeople for some reason, yet the situation where “there are still companions who believe in and rely on the protagonist” can be quite compelling.
texts.もちろん、様々な問題を解決する中で、町人からの信頼を得ていくという王道スタイルも: Of course, the classic approach of earning the townspeople's trust by solving various problems is also a good one.
texts.主人公以外の仲間に関しても、同じようにして良好な人間関係を構成させよう。感動的な: The same approach should be used to create good relationships among the companions other than the protagonist. Building warm bonds among the companions is important for achieving a moving ending. I will discuss specific ways to structure these relationships in more detail later.
texts.主人公が空気: A Protagonist Who Fades into the Background
texts.『活躍する主人公』『周りから好かれる主人公』の正反対。主人公に感情移入していたプ: The exact opposite of “a protagonist who takes center stage” and “a protagonist who is loved by those around them.” Players who had empathized with the protagonist are sure to feel empty. This requires particular caution in works with a silent protagonist and lots of conversations between companions.
texts.これを書いてる当人も若干空気主人公をやらかしている気がしないでもないです。まずっ: I have a feeling that I, the person writing this, have also made the protagonist fade into the background to some extent. If I have made a mistake, please treat me as a cautionary example.
texts.序盤～中盤に、後の展開への布石としてやるのは問題ないと思う。しかし、物語終盤にな: I think this is fine in the early to middle part of the story as groundwork for later developments. However, please spare me relationships that are still awkward near the end of the story.
texts.パーティ内でカップル成立。しかし主人公は一人孤独: A Couple Forms within the Party, Leaving the Protagonist Alone
texts.言うまでもなく心理的にかなり嫌な状況。リア充爆発しろ。: Needless to say, this is a psychologically unpleasant situation. Damn those happy couples.
texts.このように仲間同士に強すぎる絆を設定すると、主人公が空気化する懸念も。主人公にも: If you establish bonds that are too strong between the companions, as in this example, the protagonist may fade into the background. It would be best to give the protagonist some kind of bond as well.
texts.物語当初から成立している相思相愛の恋愛関係: A Mutual Romantic Relationship Established from the Beginning of the Story
texts.主人公とヒロイン等の恋愛関係が、物語開始時点で既に成立していた場合の問題点。これ: This is the problem that arises when a romantic relationship between the protagonist and heroine, for example, is already established when the story begins. From the protagonist's perspective, one might think, “What's wrong with being popular?” But it does not work that way from the player's perspective. It carries a considerable risk of preventing players from empathizing with the characters.
texts.長い物語を進める中で、主人公とヒロインは仲を深めていくのが正道。: The proper approach is for the protagonist and heroine to grow closer as the long story unfolds.
texts.その過程を体験することで、プレイヤーは主人公やヒロインに感情移入をしたり、好意を: By experiencing that process, players empathize with the protagonist and heroine and develop affection for them. Portraying this part is quite difficult, and it is not uncommon for an entire work to be criticized because “I hate the heroine.”
texts.ただでさえ、恋愛関係の描写は扱いが難しいのだが、当初から、主人公とヒロインの関係: Portraying romantic relationships is difficult enough as it is, but the problem becomes even more serious when the relationship between the protagonist and heroine is already established from the beginning.
texts.なんせ、大事な部分の過程を無視することになる。: After all, this means skipping over the process that matters most.
texts.当然、プレイヤーは主人公程にはヒロインのことを好きになれない可能性が高くなるし、: Naturally, players are then less likely to come to love the heroine as much as the protagonist does, and it also becomes difficult for them to empathize with a protagonist who loves her.
texts.開始時点での主人公とヒロインの関係は、仲が良い幼馴染ぐらいが無難と思う。……そも: At the beginning, it seems safest for the protagonist and heroine to be no more than close childhood friends. …Though there is no need to force romance into the story in the first place.
texts.物語当初からのリア充: A Protagonist Who Already Has It All from the Start
texts.同様の理由で、主人公が物語開始時点で既に多くの仲間キャラと親しい、といったリア充: For the same reason, it is difficult to make the protagonist someone who is already close to many companion characters when the story begins—a protagonist who already has it all.
texts.やはり、過程を飛ばした人間関係はプレイヤー目線では感情移入し辛い。それに、余りに: As expected, relationships that skip the process of becoming close are difficult for players to empathize with. Besides, if there are too many companions from the start, players will get tired trying to keep track of them all. It is fine to have some companions who are already close to the protagonist, such as siblings or childhood friends, but two or three should be enough.
texts.余談だけど、ＲＰＧの主人公に１０～２０代が多いのは、対象プレイヤーの年齢を考慮し: As an aside, the reason RPG protagonists are often in their teens or twenties is, of course, partly due to the target players' ages. But I think the bigger reasons are that younger, unformed people are “easier to empathize with” and that “having less background information makes the introduction smoother.”
texts.もっとも、３０代以降の主人公を全否定するわけでもない。: That said, I am not rejecting protagonists in their thirties or older outright.
texts.少し表現が難しくなるかもしれないが、人がやらないことをやるのは差別化にもなる。影: It may be somewhat difficult to portray, but doing something others do not is also a way to stand out. A sufficiently viable premise would be to make the protagonist a battle-hardened swordsman with a troubled past, which is gradually revealed as the story progresses.
texts.仲間キャラクターには明確な個性付けを: Give Your Party Members Distinct Personalities
texts.仲間キャラクターには明確な個性付けをした上で、それぞれの個性は分散させよう。色々: Give your party members clear, distinct personalities, and make sure those personalities are varied. Having a diverse cast broadens the scope of the story and adds flair. It also gives the author more creative options.
texts.また、性格に特徴のないキャラクターや、似たような性格のキャラクターが集まると、単: Also, when characters with no notable personality traits or with similar personalities are gathered together, they naturally become difficult to distinguish.
texts.セリフも各自の口調や一人称（俺、僕、私、あたし……）を分散させた方が、すぐに見分: Their speech patterns and first-person pronouns (I, me, etc.) should also be varied, making them easy to tell apart and the story easier to read. Whether in novels or games, works where it takes time to figure out who said each line are painful to experience.
texts.各キャラクターの個性付けは、基本的には『熱血』『冷静』『お転婆』『温厚』『博識』: Character personalities can basically be based on simple categories such as “hot-blooded,” “calm,” “tomboyish,” “gentle,” “knowledgeable,” “weak-willed,” “airheaded,” and “taciturn.” From there, whether you can give those personalities depth depends on the author’s skill.
texts.「単純な分類」＝「安直なキャラ付け」というわけではないので注意したい。: Keep in mind that “simple categories” do not necessarily mean “superficial characterization.”
texts.例えば、いくら熱血キャラだからといっても「敵に真正面から突っ込んで、事態を悪化さ: For example, no matter how hot-blooded a character is, if they repeatedly charge straight at the enemy and make matters worse without learning from their mistakes, you will eventually grow tired of it. It might work for a comedic character, though…
texts.あくまでも人間として、自然な思考や行動をさせることが原則。: The basic principle is to have them think and act naturally, as human beings.
texts.各キャラが取る言動は「自分ならどうする？」を基準にすればよいと思う。そこから、余: I think the standard for each character’s words and actions should be, “What would I do?” Even for a fictional character, it is probably safest not to have them casually say or do things that are too far removed from that.
texts.物語を動かすために、時には強引な行動をさせる必要もあるかもしれないが、そのポイン: You may sometimes need to have characters take forceful actions to move the story forward, but try to limit those instances. For example, early on, you can deliberately have a character say or do something that turns the player against them in order to portray their immaturity.
texts.また、別にプレイヤーに嫌われてもよいキャラクターならば、割りきって、ストーリーの: On the other hand, if a character is not meant to be liked by the players, you might as well have them do whatever they want to suit the needs of the story.
texts.具体的に、どのようにパーティの人間関係を構成していくかを考える。大事なのは各キャ: Let’s consider specifically how to structure relationships within the party. The important thing is to distribute each character’s role so that none of them overlap. I came up with two approaches.
texts.家族に例えて構成する: Structure the Party as a Family
texts.パーティメンバーの年齢がバラバラの場合は、それぞれを家族に当てはめると、バランス: When the party members vary in age, assigning each of them a family role creates a well-balanced group.
texts.主人公とヒロインを中心に見て、各仲間が以下のようなポジションに当てはまるように構: Centering on the protagonist and heroine, assign each companion one of the following positions to help prevent their roles from overlapping.
texts.パーティの中心として皆を主導する。: Leads everyone as the center of the party.
texts.パーティで年長の男性。: The oldest man in the party.
texts.物語のキーマンとして、パーティを監督する率が高い気がする。: As a key figure in the story, he often seems to supervise the party.
texts.パーティで年長の女性。: The oldest woman in the party.
texts.あんまり出てこない。: She does not appear very often.
texts.主人公より年上の男性。: A man older than the protagonist.
texts.父に近い役割を果たすこともあれば、親友格だったりする場合も。: Sometimes he serves a role similar to the father’s, while in other cases he is more like a best friend.
texts.ヒロインより年上の女性。: A woman older than the heroine.
texts.冷静な知恵役だったり、姉御肌だったり。: She may be the calm, wise one or have a protective big-sister personality.
texts.主人公より年下の男性。: A man younger than the protagonist.
texts.ヤンチャだったり、いじられ役だったり。: He may be mischievous or serve as the butt of jokes.
texts.ヒロインより年下の女性。: A woman younger than the heroine.
texts.ムードメーカー。割りと美味しいポジション。: The mood-maker. A fairly desirable position.
texts.重要な役割を果たす異種族だったり、単なるマスコットだったりと色々と自由に設定でき: This role can be freely defined in many ways, from a member of another race who plays an important role to a simple mascot.
texts.以上は目安だが、最終的なパーティ人数によっても、構成は変わってくるので柔軟に考え: The above is only a guideline, and the structure will also change depending on the final party size, so be flexible. Overlapping roles, such as “father and older brother” or “mother and older sister,” are easy to combine. You can also assign the protagonist or heroine one of the older or younger sibling roles.
texts.次に役割を元にパーティ構成を考えてみる。: Next, let’s consider structuring the party around roles.
texts.とりあえずは、下のような感じで分類してみた。分類名の一部は良い言葉がなかったので: For now, I classified them roughly as shown below. I came up with some of the category names arbitrarily because I could not find better terms. Along with the family-based structure, let’s give each character an appropriate role.
texts.プレイヤーの視点となる人物。: The character who serves as the player’s point of view.
texts.基本は主人公だがＤＱ４のように進行に応じて変化する場合も。: Usually this is the protagonist, but it may change as the story progresses, as in Dragon Quest IV.
texts.シャーロック・ホームズにおけるワトスンのように、物語の中心から外れた人物に固定す: In some cases, this role is fixed to a character outside the center of the story, like Watson in Sherlock Holmes, but by its nature, it is ill-suited to RPGs.
texts.物語の目的に最も強く関わる人物。: The character most strongly connected to the purpose of the story.
texts.主人公あるいはヒロイン。西遊記では三蔵法師に当たる。: The protagonist or heroine. In Journey to the West, this role is played by Xuanzang.
texts.物語の目的を果たすために、実際にパーティを主導しながら活躍する人物。: The character who actively contributes while actually leading the party in order to fulfill the purpose of the story.
texts.ＲＰＧにおいては、プレイヤーが操作するキャラクター（＝主観者）に等しい場合が普通: In RPGs, this role is usually equivalent to the character controlled by the player (i.e., the viewpoint character). Naturally, it would be a problem if the protagonist did not fill this role. A classic setup is for the protagonist to work hard to fulfill the purpose held by the heroine in the “purpose role.”
texts.直接パーティを主導しないが、主人公を初めとしたパーティメンバーを指導・補佐する役: A character who does not directly lead the party, but guides and supports the party members, including the protagonist.
texts.主人公（またはヒロイン）に付き従う者。: Someone who follows the protagonist (or heroine).
texts.主人公の身分が高い場合は文字通りの従者（護衛やメイドなど）がいることが多い。その: When the protagonist has high social status, they often have literal attendants, such as guards or maids. This category can also include younger brothers or sisters and underlings.
texts.物事に対して感想を述べる役割。それによって、プレイヤーが話に付いて行きやすいよう: A character whose role is to comment on events. This makes it easier for the player to follow the story.
texts.思ったことを、そのまま口にするような率直なキャラのほうがよいかも。: A straightforward character who says exactly what they think may work best.
texts.問題を整理・解決するために知恵を出す役目。: The character whose role is to provide wisdom for organizing and solving problems.
texts.冷静な分析をするタイプもいれば、科学等の技術によって物事を解決するタイプも。『感: Some are the type to perform calm analyses, while others solve problems through science and other technologies. Exchanges with the “commentator” often help explain the situation to the player in an easy-to-understand way.
texts.感想役「どういうことだってばよ！？」: Commentator: “What the heck does that mean!?”
texts.「故意にイタズラする」「うかつな行動を取る」などして物語を引っ掻き回す。: They stir up the story by doing things such as “deliberately playing pranks” or “acting carelessly.”
texts.高い行動力で、既存の秩序を破壊し、新たな局面を導き出すという主人公属性的な側面も: They also have an aspect of the protagonist archetype: through their high initiative, they destroy the existing order and bring about a new turn of events.
texts.最初は敵側として登場するキャラなどによいかも。: This may work well for a character who initially appears on the enemy’s side, for example.
texts.物語の進行には関わらないところで、物語・会話を盛り上げる役目を持つ。明るいキャラ: This character’s role is to liven up the story and conversations outside the actual progression of the plot. It is a chance for the cheerful character to shine.
texts.『いじられ役』などもこれに含んでよいかも。: The “butt of the joke” role may also fit into this category.
texts.一つのキャラクターが複数の役割を持つ場合もあれば、複数のキャラクターが一つの役目: Sometimes one character has multiple roles, while other times multiple characters share a single role. However, it is best not to have too many characters overlap in their roles.
texts.また、物語が進むに連れて役割が移っていくことも多い。例えば、最初は未熟で『主観者: Roles also often shift as the story progresses. For example, as an initially inexperienced protagonist who was nothing more than a “viewpoint character” grows, they may become a “leader” who guides their companions.
texts.「うまく役割を与えられなかったキャラ」や「仲の良い相手がいないキャラ」「戦闘で使: Be careful, because “characters who were not given suitable roles,” “characters who have no close relationships,” and “characters who are not used in battle” tend to fade into the background. Characters who appear particularly late are likely to be treated unfairly, losing out to earlier characters in terms of “roles,” “friendships,” and “combat.”
texts.ＤＱ７～８の『話す』やテイルズオブの『チャット』など、本筋を進めるには必要でない: Some games incorporate conversations with party members that are not necessary for progressing the main story as a system, such as the “Talk” feature in DQ7–8 and the “Skits” in Tales of games. This is one way to emphasize the characters’ personalities. For those unfamiliar with them, here is a brief explanation…
texts.主人公が仲間から話を聞き出すという一対一の会話。無口主人公ならば、選択肢を除いて: A one-on-one conversation in which the protagonist draws information out of a party member. With a silent protagonist, aside from choices, the conversation becomes one-way, with the party member doing all the talking. Since a silent protagonist cannot participate in “Skits,” this option is naturally recommended.
texts.複数の仲間同士でのワイワイした会話。パーティ内での関係性・仲の良さなどを強調する: Lively conversations among multiple party members. These can emphasize the relationships and friendships within the party.
texts.いずれにせよ、作業量は半端ないので注意。長編ＲＰＧでこんなシステムを導入すると、: In any case, be warned that the amount of work involved is enormous. If you introduce a system like this in a long RPG, the total amount of text, including the main story, will almost certainly exceed the length of a novel (150,000 characters or more).
texts.漫画などは連載が続く中で、無闇にキャラが増加する傾向がある。: Manga and similar works tend to add characters indiscriminately as serialization continues.
texts.結果、存在感のないキャラが増えたり、無理に全員に見せ場を作って、テンポが悪くなる: As a result, they may end up with more characters who lack presence, or the pacing may suffer because the creators force themselves to give every character a chance to shine. Games are not serialized, so this is not something you need to worry about. Consider the overall structure and determine which members are necessary.
